phrase.text: A variable that is declared and never used, or written and never read, produces a warning: the program works, but something is left over.

runs.text: A variable that is declared and never used, or written and never read, produces a warning: the program works, but something is left over.
The engine tells two oversights apart:
: they do not prevent running. They usually point to a misspelt name, a result someone forgot to show or a leftover from an earlier version.

diagnostics.message: Variable declared but never used: olvidada
Variable assigned but never read: escrita

runs.text: Parameters and subprograms nobody uses have their own warnings, with the same idea.

points.text: Declaring and not using, or writing and not reading, produces a warning.
They usually point to a name mistake or a forgotten result.
